technology.summary: Today's technology news is dominated by AI. Microsoft has announced new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes, while Google has released a new local-first Granola competitor. Nvidia is betting on physical AI to make robotaxis and humanoid robots safer. Vesta, an AI-native software startup, has raised $30 million to bring swarms of agents to mortgage lenders. Meanwhile, Uber and China's Pony.ai plan to launch robotaxis in London, and China's Manus has raised over $500 million in its first funding round since splitting with Meta.

Uber and China’s Pony.ai plan to launch robotaxis in London
China’s Manus raises over $500M in first funding round since split with Meta

finance.summary: Today's most important finance news includes the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India joining forces to simplify regulatory procedures for foreign portfolio investors. This comes as Indian equity benchmarks experience a decline due to profit booking and rising oil prices, with the Nifty 50 index closing down by 95.75 points. In other news, a landmark Supreme Court of India ruling on hospital markups for cancer drugs has led to a 5% drop in the BSE Hospitals Index. Meanwhile, a resurgent El Niño pattern threatens to deepen a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, pushing yields higher as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt.

citations.headline: Sebi, RBI join hands to make onboarding easier for FPIs
Stocks in news: Infosys, HDFC Bank, Jio Financial, IRFC, NCC and Blue Dart
Hospital stocks slip after SC query on steep cancer drug markups
El Niño to Compound Drag on Southeast Asian Debt, Analysts Say

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence, as well as the Supreme Court's decision to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai were detained, and the party has condemned the action. Meanwhile, former US President Donald Trump has cited a non-existent Indian election to call the US electoral process 'corrupt'.

citations.headline: Delhi High Court dismisses pleas for SIT probe into 2020 riots, 2019 Jamia violence
Supreme Court to list plea to allow peaceful protests  to Jantar Mantar
Congress claims tribal students headed for Mumbai protest detained; condemns action
Trump cites Indian election that didn't happen to call U.S. electoral process ‘corrupt’
